record.original_question: Find an interesting (nonselfdajoint resp. nonsymmetric) model problem, where the theoretical result on the eigenvalue distribution of the preconditioned matrix indeed corresponds to the actual convergence behavior of GMRES (e.g., $M^-1A$ has $m$ eigenvalue clusters and an acceptable approximate solution is obtained by GMRES in $ O(m)$ steps). Determine which particular properties of the problem implied this correspondence.

evidence.quote: Find an interesting (nonselfdajoint resp. nonsymmetric) model problem, where the theoretical result on the eigenvalue distribution of the preconditioned matrix indeed corresponds to the actual convergence behavior of GMRES (e.g., $M^{-1}A$ has $m$ eigenvalue clusters and an acceptable approximate solution is obtained by GMRES in ${\cal O}(m)$ steps). Determine which particular properties of the problem implied this correspondence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a nonsingular, non-Hermitian (nonsymmetric) matrix and let $M \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a nonsingular preconditioner. Consider the linear system $Ax = b$ solved by the (left) preconditioned GMRES method applied to $M^{-1}A x = M^{-1}b$, starting from $x_0 = 0$, which at step $k$ produces the iterate $x_k$ minimizing $\|M^{-1}(b - A x_k)\|_2$ over the Krylov subspace $\mathcal{K}_k(M^{-1}A, M^{-1}b)$.

Suppose the spectrum $\sigma(M^{-1}A)$ can be partitioned into $m$ clusters, i.e., there exist $m$ points $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m \in \mathbb{C}$ (bounded away from $0$) and a small radius $\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$$\sigma(M^{-1}A) \subset \bigcup_{j=1}^{m} D(\lambda_j, \varepsilon),$$
where $D(\lambda,\varepsilon)$ denotes the closed disk of radius $\varepsilon$ around $\lambda$.

Task: Exhibit a concrete and mathematically interesting non-Hermitian model problem $(A, M)$ — for instance arising from the discretization of a non-self-adjoint partial differential or integral operator together with a natural preconditioner — for which the following correspondence between the spectral clustering of $M^{-1}A$ and the actual convergence behavior of GMRES provably holds: an acceptable approximate solution (i.e., relative residual below a prescribed tolerance independent of $n$) is obtained in $\mathcal{O}(m)$ GMRES iterations, with constants independent of the discretization parameter. Identify and rigorously justify which structural properties of the problem (e.g., normality or near-normality of $M^{-1}A$, bounds on the field of values, departure from normality, conditioning of the eigenvector basis, regularity of the underlying continuous operator, or bounds on pseudospectra) are responsible for ensuring that the eigenvalue clustering translates into the predicted GMRES convergence rate.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open-ended research desideratum asking for example problems where eigenvalue-cluster-based GMRES convergence bounds are sharp, together with identification of the structural properties responsible. The literature (e.g., Greenbaum–Pták–Strakoš 1996 showing that any nonincreasing residual curve can correspond to any spectrum) emphasizes that eigenvalues alone do not determine GMRES convergence in the nonnormal case, and partial answers exist for nearly normal operators or via field-of-values/pseudospectra arguments. No definitive resolution is recorded; the problem appears to remain open as stated.

status_evidence.title: Any nonincreasing convergence curve is possible for GMRES
status_evidence.snippet: Greenbaum, Pták, and Strakoš show that the eigenvalues of A alone do not determine the convergence behavior of GMRES.
status_evidence.claim: Eigenvalue distribution alone is insufficient to characterize GMRES convergence in general, motivating the search for problem classes where clustering does dictate convergence.
